title: This tech job is in huge demand right now, Cursor's head of talent says
excerpt: Matt Ward, Cursor's head of talent, said forward-deployed engineers are the most in-demand role in tech right now.
content_html:
By Lakshmi Varanasi

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Someone needs to teach all the businesses out there how to use AI. Enter the so-called forward-deployed engineer.

Matt Ward, Cursor's head of talent, said on a recent episode of the "People by WTF" podcast that companies are racing to hire forward-deployed engineers to help companies and their clients adopt and personalize AI.

"You're deeply technical yourself," Ward said, describing the type of person who is a good fit for the job. "But you can also walk into a room with executives and leaders."

The role, popularized by Palantir, sits somewhere between software engineering, consulting, and product. Forward-deployed engineers typically integrate with customers, learn how their businesses operate, and then build or customize technology to meet their needs.

Demand for the role has exploded during the AI boom. Job postings for forward-deployed engineers in April were up over 5,000% compared to last year, according to Indeed data.

Several major AI companies are building dedicated teams around them. OpenAI's forward-deployed engineering team had 39 members late last year and 24 openings across the US, Europe, and Japan. Salaries for the role at OpenAI can be as high as $345,000 plus equity.

As AI companies race to turn powerful models into products businesses can actually use, it's not just engineers who are bridging the gap between technology and customers. Consultants are too.

Consulting firms have been hiring and retraining workers to help clients figure out where AI fits within their businesses and how to deploy it.

BCG, for example, has created a team of "forward-deployed consultants" who can vibe code and build AI tools directly on client projects, while McKinsey is increasingly looking for hires who can combine strong consulting skills with technical fluency.

作者：Lakshmi Varanasi 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

需要有人教所有企业如何使用人工智能。 所谓的前沿部署工程师登场了。

Cursor 的人才主管马特·沃德 (Matt Ward) 在最近一期的“People by WTF”播客中表示，公司正在竞相聘请前沿部署的工程师，以帮助公司及其客户采用和个性化人工智能。

“你自己技术性很强，”沃德在描述适合这份工作的人类型时说道。 “但你也可以走进一个有高管和领导者的房间。”

Palantir 推广的这个职位介于软件工程、咨询和产品之间。 前沿部署的工程师通常与客户集成，了解他们的业务如何运作，然后构建或定制技术来满足他们的需求。

在人工智能热潮期间，对该职位的需求激增。 根据 Indeed 数据，4 月份前沿部署工程师的职位发布量比去年增加了 5,000% 以上。

几家主要的人工智能公司正在围绕它们建立专门的团队。 去年年底，OpenAI 的前沿部署工程团队共有 39 名成员，并在美国、欧洲和日本开设了 24 个职位空缺。 OpenAI 该职位的薪资加上股权可高达 345,000 美元。

随着人工智能公司竞相将强大的模型转化为企业可以实际使用的产品，弥合技术和客户之间差距的不仅仅是工程师。 顾问也是。

咨询公司一直在招聘和再培训员工，以帮助客户找出人工智能在其业务中的适合位置以及如何部署它。

例如，BCG 创建了一支“前沿部署顾问”团队，他们可以直接在客户项目上编写代码并构建人工智能工具，而麦肯锡则越来越多地寻找能够将强大的咨询技能与技术流畅性结合起来的员工。
